A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Density Guidance work. Their text, equations, figures, and complete appendices are readable and can be matched across renumbering and relocation.

before.justification: V1 reports original score-alignment measurements, image-detail correlations, generated-image comparisons, and Gaussian-mixture and image-data analyses.

after.justification: V2 retains those empirical results and adds quantile-matching accuracy experiments, quantitative guidance comparisons, and NIQE evaluations.

M1.justification: Prior Guidance, score-alignment verification, deterministic Density Guidance, and the stochastic projection and drift corrections are retained. The new experiments apply existing procedures; the Rayleigh-quotient shorthand does not change the stochastic method.

E1.justification: Both versions cover CIFAR-10, ImageNet at 64 and 512 resolution, Stable Diffusion text-to-image generation, and synthetic Gaussian mixtures. The additions evaluate retained coverage; classifier-free guidance changes the model configuration rather than the dataset or task.

E2.justification: V2 adds Prior Guidance to the early/late stochastic-noise comparison in Figure 19 and regular samples as a reference in the NIQE comparison in Figure 20. The existing FLIPD comparison remains unchanged. LPIPS and SSIM are discussed but not evaluated.

E3.justification: New protocols include deterministic and stochastic sampling-step sweeps, quantile-estimation sample counts from 16 to 1024, noise strengths of 0.1, 0.5, and 0.9 times the diffusion strength, and a 1024-step reference likelihood estimate. V2 also adds classifier-free-guidance evaluation and NIQE scoring. These substantially expand evaluation without replacing the retained protocols.

E4.justification: Appendices E and H newly test whether requested likelihoods are reached and how discretization, quantile-estimation sample size, and stochastic noise affect accuracy. Appendices J–L add guidance-strength analyses, classifier-free-guidance compatibility, stochastic Prior Guidance comparisons, and perceptual-quality analysis.

E5.justification: Figure 19 newly specifies two starting seeds, four stochastic samples per seed, and shared inner-loop seeds across runs. New quantitative plots include error bars, although their statistical meaning is not defined. The retained normality tests and reported plus/minus values are unchanged.

E6.justification: V2 adds target-versus-obtained likelihood results, reporting correlations above 99% even with 32 deterministic Euler steps, and shows greater sampling requirements under stronger noise. Figures 16–20 add measured detail, likelihood, and NIQE trends. Existing results, including 97%/100% score alignment and 84% versus 29% detail correlations, are retained; these are additional results rather than same-setting performance gains over v1.

T1.justification: Section 2.2 corrects the forward Gaussian kernel's covariance from sigma_t I to sigma_t^2 I. The score-alignment proofs, Gaussian-mixture theorem, and density-guidance derivations otherwise remain intact. Rewriting the stochastic derivation using the existing Rayleigh quotient introduces no new theoretical result.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same contributions: explaining Prior Guidance through score alignment, controlling log-density through deterministic guidance, and extending control to stochastic sampling. New experiments support these claims without redefining their scope.

C2.justification: V2 discusses finite-step accuracy and the additional sampling required under stronger stochastic noise. It also explains Prior Guidance's weakening control as noise reduces information from the initial latent, and notes that NIQE favors lower-detail images. These add practical qualifications to the retained interpretations.

D1.justification: V2 adds a code-repository link and documents implementation details for the new experiments, including Euler integration, moving-average finite-difference estimation of quantile derivatives, and early/late noise schedules. The existing JAX score-alignment listing is unchanged.

R1.justification: V2 adds Skreta et al. to the attribution of generalized density tracking and cites NIQE, LPIPS, SSIM, and a diffusion super-resolution application when motivating perceptual evaluation. The main research positioning is retained; the Karczewski citation's year update refers to the same work.

P1.justification: The main narrative and section order remain largely unchanged. V2 adds short experimental appendices and acknowledgements, updates cross-references, makes limited wording edits, and renames Appendix D from likelihood steering to Density Guidance.

P2.justification: V2 substantially expands the appendix displays with multi-panel convergence plots, paired image-and-metric comparisons, stochastic sampling grids, and NIQE plots and examples in Figures 12 and 15–20. Existing figures are largely retained, with some relocated and renumbered.

improvement.justification: V1 supplied theoretical guarantees and qualitative detail control but lacked direct quantitative validation of reaching requested likelihoods. V2's Appendices E and H address that central evidence gap and expose discretization and noise dependence; additional detail and perceptual comparisons strengthen practical validation. Together with documented code access, this substantially improves the paper's empirical grounding. Undefined error bars and NIQE's preference for smoother images still limit statistical and perceptual conclusions.
